turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we'll be efficient. My son found out about a zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Tell me why that happened.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
I didn't come to be thanked, Hale. I came to hear the zero withdrawn. Are you prepared to do that today?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
That's a machine's guess, Hale. The company that sells it says in print that it shouldn't be the sole basis for acting against a student. What else do you have?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." A study of fourteen detection tools called them "neither accurate nor reliable," and I've read it. Procedure 4.3 in your own school's policy says software alone doesn't establish a concern, so show me something that isn't software.
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, and 4.2 says you call me before any mark is entered. Did you do either one?
I hope you understand my position.
"I hope." My position is the zero comes off, and you haven't told me whether anyone called me or spoke to Owen before it went in. Answer that, Hale.
